verdict.headline: Iran deal collapses after Trump demands compensation from Tehran, sending oil past both price triggers
verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — 3/6 regime breached: WTI $82.13 (above $79 trigger), Brent $87.72 (above $85), 30Y at 5.25%. September hike odds 51% (CME) and rising. SPX futures +0.1% mask compounding oil-rate risk; July CPI Wednesday Aug 12 at 8:30 AM ET is the sole clearing event.
verdict.horizon: 24-48 hours — through Wednesday August 12 CPI at 8:30 AM ET
verdict.rationale_short: Both oil regime triggers breached simultaneously on Aug 10: WTI settled at $82.13 (+4.2% from $78.72), Brent at $87.72 (+3.9% from $84.39). The catalyst was a decisive pivot in the Iran negotiating track — Trump told Axios on Sunday the US is 'only semi-negotiating' with Iran, then directed US representatives to demand financial compensation FROM Tehran, conditions that directly reverse the Oman framework and that Iran flatly rejected. Iranian FM Araghchi confirmed no direct US-Iran talks are underway. The 30Y extended to 5.253% (+17bps from yesterday's 5.08%), and September hike odds moved from 44% to ~51%. Three of six regime indicators are now in active breach. SPX futures are +0.1% this morning and Nasdaq futures +0.4% — the equity market has not priced the oil-rate compounding — creating asymmetric setup into Wednesday's CPI. July headline consensus: 3.4% YoY (down from 3.5%), core 2.5% (down from 2.6%); prediction markets lean tame. A soft print clears oil from the immediate rate narrative and drops September odds back below 35%; a hot print (above 3.5% headline or 2.7% core) activates the fourth breach (September above 70%) and introduces simultaneous rate-and-supply pressure into the Aug 20 SPCX tranche at $133. Do not add exposure ahead of the print.

trade_setups.asset: July CPI — Wednesday August 12, 8:30 AM ET (regime binary)
trade_setups.thesis: With Brent at $87.72 and WTI at $82.13 having already breached their regime thresholds, Wednesday's CPI is now a three-way binary: (1) soft (headline ≤3.3%, core ≤2.4%): September odds drop from 51% to below 35%, 30Y retreats from 5.25%, oil decouples from the rate narrative — regime clears to 2/6, full recovery thesis intact; (2) in-line (headline 3.4%, core 2.5%): September stays ~45-50%, 30Y holds ~5.20-5.25%, Jackson Hole Aug 27 decides the medium-term; (3) hot (headline ≥3.5%, core ≥2.7%): September hike probability crosses 70%, activating a fourth breach and triggering simultaneous rate-and-supply pressure into the Aug 20 SPCX tranche. July embeds a Brent average near $82-88/bbl — the same range driving today's oil surge — creating genuine upside risk to the 3.4% headline consensus.
trade_setups.entry: Pre-CPI tells: 30Y above 5.30% by Tuesday afternoon signals bond market pre-pricing a hot read. DXY above 100.50 confirms rate re-escalation is being priced. September hike odds above 58% by Tuesday close would be the formal pre-print warning.
trade_setups.invalidation: CPI within ±0.1% of consensus (in-line scenario) leaves September unresolved through Jackson Hole (Aug 27).
trade_setups.horizon: 24 hours — Wednesday August 12 at 8:30 AM ET

trade_setups.thesis: Both oil regime triggers breached simultaneously Monday: WTI $82.13 (above $79, +$3.41 from trigger), Brent $87.72 (above $85, +$2.72 from trigger). The collapse of the Oman routing framework eliminates the near-term de-escalation scenario; Trump's compensation-from-Iran demand is publicly committed and Iran has publicly rejected it. The deal has now failed to close four times in 2026. A continuation toward WTI $85 / Brent $93 would constitute a second leg requiring defensive positioning in energy-exposed sectors. The one reversal catalyst — a sudden US policy reversal on compensation terms — is unlikely given public commitments. Brent above $93 would embed oil-driven inflation directly into the Q3 CPI series.
trade_setups.entry: Regime active at WTI $82.13 / Brent $87.72. Next level that changes the read upward: Brent $93 (second-leg signal, Q3 CPI contamination); downward: WTI below $79 on a verified US-Iran deal (regime clears).
trade_setups.invalidation: A formally signed agreement addressing Trump's compensation terms and Iran's Hormuz conditions compresses WTI below $73 and clears the oil breach.
trade_setups.horizon: Days to 2 weeks; reassess post-CPI Wednesday

bear_case: Both WTI ($82.13) and Brent ($87.72) have breached their regime thresholds simultaneously — the exact scenario Monday's briefing identified as the highest-risk event before Wednesday's CPI. The 30Y has extended to 5.253%, adding 17bps from yesterday, and September hike odds have climbed from 44% to 51%. Three of six regime indicators are now in active breach. The compounding danger arrives Wednesday: July CPI embeds a Brent average near $82-88/bbl, creating genuine upside risk to the 3.4% headline consensus. A print above 3.5% headline or 2.7% core would push September hike odds toward 70%, triggering the fourth breach and introducing simultaneous rate-and-supply pressure for SPCX's Aug 20 tranche at $133 — the highest-beta downside scenario across the watchlist. SPX at 7,760 near records while three regime indicators are actively breached is the structural mismatch defining today's risk: the index has not priced oil-rate compounding. If SPX loses 7,650 on a daily close before Wednesday, the hold thesis is fully broken and defensive repositioning becomes non-optional.
